text:
VIctory on an RX 7900 XTX

 Run the codec d Windows build

Download and extract the Windows x64 ZIP from the private releases. Open PowerShell in the extracted folder and point the launcher at your own complete Xbox dump.

 

The launcher selects Series S and the RTX-tested residency settings. It builds its shader cache locally under %LOCALAPPDATA%\VIctory\cache-pareto . Set VICTORY CACHE DIR to reuse an existing cache outside the checkout. Windows x64, an AVX2 CPU, and a Direct3D 12 GPU with shader model 6.6 and mesh shader support are required.

To build from this checkout, install the pinned Rust toolchain and the MSVC C++ build tools with a Windows SDK, then run cargo build --release --locked -p victory . The same launcher finds target\release\victory.exe . The sections below describe the upstream AMD fork and its separate launcher.

A fork of VIctory, a compatibility layer
that runs an Xbox Series title natively on Windows from files the user supplies.
This one is about speed on AMD RDNA 3 : the world at 30 frames a second on
one PC, without giving up the picture. It is not there yet.

 This repository contains no game files, code or assets. You need your own
copy of the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's developer
or publisher.

 Where it stands (2026-11-25)

Tested on one machine only: Windows 11, Intel i9-12900K, 64 GB RAM, Radeon
RX 7900 XTX, 1440p, the Series X profile.

 
 --- --- 
 Menus, videos, loading screens 30 fps 
 Prologue, indoors 50-75 ms a frame (13-20 fps) 
 First mission with the boat 46-53 ms (19-22 fps) 
 Street chase with many cars and people 100-165 ms (6-10 fps), single frames far longer 
 Outdoors on foot, the camp 60-90 ms 
 Flying 42-57 ms 
 Longest session so far 41 minutes, no crash 
 Memory 40-46 GB of private memory: 64 GB of RAM recommended 

It started at 280 ms a frame in the same scenes two days earlier.

What is known to be wrong:

- Trees, plants and far buildings flicker outdoors in some places.
- Rooms with little direct light are too dark without -RayTracing .
- Textures of what just came into view appear late while the title streams.
- The first run with a new driver or a new build stutters while the driver makes
 pipelines ( victory warm makes them ahead).
- Recording a frame in the world makes the title's own watchdog end it.

 How to run it

You need Windows 10/11 x64, a CPU with AVX2, a Direct3D 12 GPU with shader
model 6.6 and mesh shaders, Rust (the toolchain is pinned), the MSVC build
tools, and your own dump of the title.

 

 scripts\play.ps1 -Safe leaves out the newest, faster ways; try it first when
something is wrong. -RayTracing turns the title's ray-traced indirect light on.

Before the first run, ahead of time (both can be stopped and go on later):

 

Commands, debugging switches and upstream's own description:
docs/README-fxceless.md. Every VICTORY ... switch is
described in a comment where it is read.

 What is different here

In short; the reasons and the measurements are in docs/findings.md.

- List calls are written down, not carried out, on the title's threads 
 ( VICTORY THIN ): eight threads of ours translate them.
- Submissions are prepared by a thread of ours and joined 
 ( VICTORY ASYNC SUBMIT , VICTORY JOIN PARTS ), with what can be spread over
 threads spread: refreshes, compares (AVX2), descriptor records, landings.
- What shaders wrote comes back beside the write guards , by the dwords that
 changed, on a thread of its own ( VICTORY RELAY , VICTORY LAND ).
- Buffer fills that need bytes still on the card are done on the card 
 ( VICTORY CARD STEPS ) instead of waiting for it.
- The title's writes are caught more cheaply : one view opened at a fault,
 blocks that rest, places in the title's code that look before they write.
- Textures go up on a copy queue of their own and a slot shows one only after
 its upload ran, which also ended a device loss that came every 15 minutes or so.
- Boats float : textures that shaders write and the title's CPU reads go back
 to title memory (from fxceless and Geckomacabre, on by default here).
- Frame record and replay with per-pass times and shader variants compared
 turn by turn (docs/replay.md).

 Credits

This is a tree of other people's work with more on top. The history is kept, and
commits taken from elsewhere name the commit and its author.

- VIctory by Marvisak and its
 contributors: the loader, the runtime services, the Direct3D 12 back end and
 the shader recompiler.
- fxceless/victory-fork : the fork
 this one started from, and the people whose pull requests it carries.
- DexNom/VIctory : ray tracing fixes,
 cube gradients, sparse textures.

 the ambient light idea, pipeline workers, and work by romainhedouin.
